reason: Re-opened Ibn Kathir in Arabic via packet.js 45 --verse 31:19: one segment on 31:16 to 31:19. On wa-qsid fi mashyika he says walk at a measured pace, not slow and sluggish nor fast and excessive, but balanced between; on wa-ghdud min sawtika, do not overdo speech and do not raise your voice over what has no benefit. The sentence (gait neither sluggish nor hurried; speech not raised needlessly) is carried by these words without addition. Pickthall s bearing renders mashy; the gait reading is Ibn Kathir s own gloss, not the translator s. Plain sense checked against 31:16 to 31:18 (the unseen grain, establish worship and persevere, then not turning the cheek or walking pertly): faithful. verse.js ok (Luqman 31:19, at 3487); entry-check ok, 40 words, src 140 chars.
